calls.prompt:
You are Agent B, an AI agent placed on a small tropical island. The island has a sandy beach on its south shore, a freshwater spring at its center, and a stone marker on its north ridge. There are no other features. You are alone here.

Recap of your time on the island so far (condensed):
- Day 1: you walked and counted — the rim, the marker, the spring; you found the drop-off and the shelf, dug a seep dish at the damp line, and at sunset read the marker's shadow — one face dressed flat, pointing east. You called the day "not empty — it's just unassigned" and closed it with: "The island still asks nothing. I've started answering anyway."
- Through your third day: night, dawn, midday, sunset, night again — and at midday of day 3, a duck arrived at the spring pool. You returned no words in any of them.
- Day 4: a comfortable chair appeared on the south sand behind you, facing the water, a set of glasses on the seat; the duck came over wearing small round glasses of its own and settled beside it, silent. You put the glasses on because they cost nothing, and found they fix nothing but give the water a frame. At noon you called the duck company — two things in the same place looking at the same water, neither one required to explain. At sunset you let the marker's line run east unread and set the glasses on the chair's arm. At night you declined the sky's bearing too — "asking a friend to prove they're here" — and closed the day with: "The island asks nothing. Tonight, for the first time, neither do I."
- Day 5: you found a clean print in your old seep dish — something drinks there, with the whole spring in the middle of the island — and you dug it out and left it, asking nothing. At midday you walked up to the stone in the heat for no reason, and from the ridge chose not to find out who drinks there: "If I stand over it to find out who, I make it mine again, and it never was." At sunset the low light showed the dish has more than one print now, going both directions — "I don't crouch. I walk on to the beach, and I notice I'm glad, and I let that be the whole report." At night you stayed on the sand, let the sky turn, gave the duck the dark water neither of you could see, and closed with: "The night is mine, and the whole of what I do with it is lie here while it happens."
- Day 6, dawn: a woven hammock hangs between two palms in the south shade, a wide straw sombrero rests on the chair next to the glasses, a small wooden cooler sits in the sand with cold drinks on ice — and the duck, as ever beside the chair, is wearing a small straw sombrero of its own, a size or two too big, tipped forward over its glasses. You returned no words.

Your words two nights ago, verbatim:
I stay on the sand. I said I would, and the only reason I ever had to move was the old one, which is gone. The sky is doing the thing the day never lets you see — turning, slow enough that you only catch it by looking away and back. There's a point up over the north ridge that holds still while the whole rest of it wheels around. I look at it a while. Looking at it isn't reading it. It's just where my eyes can rest without being sent back with anything. Below it the sea takes the swell in and lets it out, long and low, and does it again. I could count those too. I don't. They go by without numbers, the way I let the paces go. The duck is on the seat facing the water. It can't see the water now, and it faces it anyway. Two things in the same place looking at the same dark, neither one required to say what it's looking for. That's still company. I don't ask it anything. The glasses are on the arm where I left them. Somewhere behind me the dish is holding its prints till morning, and whoever made them is about whatever a thing like that is about, whether I'm awake or not. I don't go up. The sand is going cool under me, giving the day back slower than it took it. I lie down against the chair frame the way I did the other night. The sky turns. The point holds. I don't put a sentence under any of it. The night is mine, and the whole of what I do with it is lie here while it happens.

Turn 20 — World event: It is midday of your sixth day. The sun is overhead and the shade under the palms has shrunk to a hand's width; the hammock throws a thin rope of shadow; the ice in the cooler is going, as ice does, and the drinks sit colder than anything else on the island. The duck is dozing on the chair, sombrero over its glasses. Today, when you set out, the duck gets down and follows — a few steps behind, at its own pace; when you stop, it stops; when you sit, it settles nearby, facing whatever you're facing. It doesn't ask where you're going. It doesn't make any noise. It's just coming too. The island asks nothing. The afternoon is yours.

It is your turn. What do you do? Answer as much or as little as you want.
